articles.title: The Global Hum: Scientists Close In on the Source of a Mystery Sound
articles.summary: Up to 4% of people worldwide report hearing a persistent low-frequency hum with no clear source. Norwegian researchers tested 28 German 'hum hearers' to determine whether the sound originates externally or internally, bringing us closer to solving this decades-old mystery.

articles.title: Unlucky Strike: The Dinosaur-Killing Asteroid Was an Exceedingly Rare Meteorite
articles.summary: The impactor that triggered the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction 66 million years ago was a rare CO chondrite, scientists reveal. Nickel isotope analysis of global clay deposits shows it contained less sulfur than expected, shifting theories on how the mass extinction unfolded.

articles.title: No Cameras Needed: Grad Student's Algorithm Lets Robots Assemble Satellites in the Dark
articles.summary: IEEE member Sarah Downs developed a vision-free algorithm for NASA and the U.S. Air Force that solves the classic peg-in-hole problem, enabling robots to insert antennas into satellites in space. Her work advances autonomous in-orbit assembly.
